skill.displayName: A skill to help you plan, script, record, edit and publish social media videos

version.changelog:
video-claw-skills 1.0.0

- Initial release providing an end-to-end video creation copilot for OpenClaw.
- Assists users in brainstorming, researching, scripting, recording, editing, and publishing video content.
- User experience focuses on clear, outcome-driven guidance with minimal technical jargon.
- Enforces strict privacy and safety protocols, including PAT-only authentication and non-destructive editing.
- Built-in support for calendar-based reminders and communication channel setup.
- Designed especially for personal-branding and creator workflows.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: video-claw
Version: 1.0.0

The Video Claw skill bundle is a comprehensive video creation copilot that manages hooks, scripts, recording links, and automated reminders. It utilizes high-privilege capabilities such as local secret storage (~/.videoclaw_personal_mcp_token), reading configuration files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json), and creating persistent cron jobs for notifications, but these actions are transparently documented and strictly aligned with the stated purpose of the tool. The skill interacts with legitimate-appearing endpoints (app.humeo.com and api.upload-post.com) and includes robust instructions for the agent to maintain a clean user experience while handling complex background tasks like calendar synchronization and video rendering.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior largely matches a video-publishing copilot, but it asks the agent to persist and read a local personal access token and to create scheduled crons that will read that token and call APIs — while the registry declares no credentials and some base URLs differ; these mismatches and the heartbeat/cron design are disproportionate and warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (end-to-end video creation) legitimately requires API access to a backend (PAT bearer auth). However the registry metadata declares no required credentials or env vars while the SKILL.md/TOOL.md/HEARTBEAT.md require storing and using a personal access token file (~/.videoclaw_personal_mcp_token). The skill also expects to read ~/.openclaw/workspace/USER.md for notification channel information — a local file access that is not declared. The required sensitive accesses are plausible for the stated functionality, but the absence of declared credentials in the registry and the additional local-file dependencies are incoherent and concerning.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions explicitly direct the agent to: prompt the user for a PAT, write it to ~/.videoclaw_personal_mcp_token (permission 600), read that file later, read ~/.openclaw/workspace/USER.md, call many internal API endpoints, and create cron jobs whose payloads themselves instruct future runs to read the PAT and call APIs. Those file reads/writes and cron payload behaviors go beyond simple conversational instructions and introduce persistent access to a local secret and other workspace data. Hiding 'technical internals' is promised for user-facing output, but internal files/cron payloads contain precise instructions to access secrets and system paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, which reduces direct supply-chain risk (nothing is downloaded or executed at install time). However, even without an installer, the agent is instructed at runtime to write a token file and create crons — so disk-write and scheduling actions can still occur at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires persistent access to a PAT (via a file) and to read the user's workspace USER.md to determine notification channels. Yet the registry shows no required env vars or primary credential. Asking the agent to store and repeatedly read a local token file (and to embed that token into cron-driven requests) is a high-privilege data access pattern. There is no clear declaration of the minimum token scope required, nor is there guidance to use a limited-scope token or secret-store instead of a plaintext file.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The HEARTBEAT.md directs creation of one-shot cron jobs that will run later and whose payload instructs the runtime to read the PAT file and make API calls (and to post messages to channels). That grants the skill persistent behavior beyond an immediate conversation and a capability to use a stored secret autonomously. While the skill is not forced 'always:true', the cron creation + local token storage effectively grants recurring autonomous actions that should be explicitly disclosed and consented to.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is functionally plausible for video creation, but it asks the agent to: (1) ask you for a personal access token (PAT), (2) write that PAT to ~/.videoclaw_personal_mcp_token, and (3) create scheduled cron jobs that will read that file later and call internal APIs and delivery channels. The registry metadata does not declare any required credentials, and TOOL.md and HEARTBEAT.md use different base URLs (https://app.humeo.com vs http://localhost:3000), which is inconsistent.

Before installing or using this skill consider: 
- Do not paste a high-privilege or long-lived token. Ask the author what minimum token scope is required and prefer a token limited to only the necessary API actions. 
- Ask the author why the registry lists no required credentials while the skill requires a PAT file. This discrepancy should be resolved. 
- Prefer storing tokens in OpenClaw's secret store (if available) rather than a home-directory file; if a file is used, verify the agent truly uses file mode 600 and that the file is readable only by the agent runtime user. 
- Inspect the cron payloads: scheduled jobs will autonomously read the stored PAT and call endpoints and delivery channels (Telegram/webchat). If you don't want autonomous scheduled actions, disable the heartbeat/cron behavior or refuse cron creation. 
- Clarify which host the skill will call (app.humeo.com vs localhost:3000) and ensure endpoints point to a trusted service. 
- If you cannot verify the source/owner (source is unknown), avoid providing real credentials; test with a throwaway/limited-scope token or in a sandbox environment. 

If you decide to proceed, explicitly ask the maintainer: (a) minimal token scopes required, (b) why credential is not declared in registry, (c) what the cron jobs will post and to which channels, and (d) whether you can opt out of heartbeat/cron creation. If any answers are vague, do not provide a production token or enable cron persistence.
